analysis.title: Asia Open - The Fed said so
key_insights: October US core CPI printed 0.3% MoM vs 0.2% expected, driven by a broad range of subcomponents. Citi sees signs of pass-through inflation as energy prices fall.
Front-end UST yields rose 17bps and OIS priced the Jan FOMC hike at 61%.

A 50bp December hike is on the table: Fed Governor Waller said before the print that a 0.3% or higher core CPI could make a 50bp hike in December 'necessary'. Dallas Fed's Logan (2027 voter) said at least two more 25bp hikes are needed.
Citi US economists track Core PCE at +0.33%, subject to change after Friday's PPI.

US 2-year volume was roughly 150% above average. Citi's positioning expert David Bieber says larger moves are needed to force systematic rebalancing flows. Recent 10y futures longs look vulnerable below 106-00 (ref 106-06), with resistance at 108-30, leaving a near-term bias toward cheaper yields.
The $42B 10-year auction tailed the 1pm level by 0.1bp at a 5.02% yield, with a 2.46 bid/cover at the 36th percentile of the past 12 auctions.
SPX fell 38bps, NDX 60bps and RTY 68bps after morning whipsaw around CPI. Weakness was largely Nvidia (-5.5%). Breadth improved in the afternoon and VVIX dipped below 100.
Fed's Bowman flagged the risk of 'a large correction in equity valuations' stemming from AI returns.

Citi's trading strategy desk notes possible selling from Systematic Accounts. It prefers to stay invested by barbelling the 'efficient AI' basket (CGTSTOKN) with the Free Cash Flow Low Risk basket (CGTSFCFR).
DXY rose 0.60% to 102.26 following December hike odds. USDJPY nearly topped 159 for the first time since September as the US-Japan rate differential widened.
BRL and COP each weakened more than 1.2% vs the dollar. USDBRL topped 5.60 and BRL hit a near 17-month low after dovish meeting minutes. Attention is on the Finance Minister pick expected this month.

Gold fell 2.8% (-2.5% cited in the summary) and silver 3.7% on the firmer dollar. WTI fell 0.5% while TTF gas rose 6% on EU winter supply concerns. Corn rose 2% and soybeans 3% after a bigger-than-expected USDA yield and production cut.
BoC minutes leaned hawkish and Dec OIS odds rose from 40% to about 48%. Citi economists expect the BoC to hold in December. CAD was little changed.

Wednesday liquidity is expected to be light with the US bond market closed for Veterans Day. Korea 10-day exports are due at 00:00 GMT, which Citi's macro strategist says needs close watching if broad AI weakness continues.
